The Bioinformatics Research Center (BRC) administers and maintains a set of common bioinformatics software packages for the BRC community to use on Hazel. We prefer to have control over the software to reduce the burden on individual users, eliminate redundant software downloads, and control software versions for reproducibility. Software is downloaded and formatted using [container-mod](https://github.com/TuftsRT/container-mod).

## Accessing the BRC Software repository

The BRC software downloads are located in `/usr/local/usrapps/brc/brc_modules/modules`

```
brc_modules
  ├── images/    ← .sif container images
  ├── modules/   ← TCL module files
  └── tools/     ← Program executables
```

These software containers can be loaded in two different ways:

::: {.callout-important}
Do not copy this folder! Instead have your scripts/jobs point to software contained here.
:::

### Loading modules (recommended)

Much like how common modules can be loaded using `module load <module_name>`, the BRC software exists as modules in `/usr/local/usrapps/brc/brc_modules/modules`. The difference is that the `module load` command doesn't know to search in this directory. To make these modules available, you must first run:

```bash
$ module use /usr/local/usrapps/brc/brc_modules/modules/
```

Now if you run `module avail` you should see a list of all the available BRC modules at the top.

```bash
$ module avail
------------------ /usr/local/usrapps/brc/brc_modules/modules ------------------
angsd/0.940             funannotate/1.8.17          paml/4.10.10
augustus/3.5.0          gatk4/4.6.2.0                picard/3.4.0
autodock-vina/1.1.2     gcta/1.94.1                  plink2/2.00a5.12
bbtools/39.84           gffread/0.12.9               prokka/1.15.6
bcftools/1.23.1         gtdbtk/2.7.2                 raxml-ng/2.0.1
...
```

Now load any BRC module:

```bash
$ module load samtools/
Loading samtools/1.23.1
  Loading requirement: singularity/1.4.2-1
```

To use software modules in job that you submit to slurm, place the `module load` command into your job scripts -- note that whatever modules that you've loaded interactively on the login node may not make it into your job submission.

::: {.callout-warning}
The `module use` command must be run every time you log onto hazel for the BRC modules to be available. You can edit your `.bashrc` profile to automatically run `module use` upon start up.
:::

#### test
In most cases, when you load a BRC module, you are actually running that software inside a container. Therefore, you may experience **bind path** issues if you reference data that is not in your current directory. If this is an issue, you will often see an error telling you files don't exist (e.g. `[E::hts_open] fail to open file`). See the **Bind paths and file visibility** section below for more information.

### Using apptainer

You may also run software without loading it as a module by using the apptainer tool. First load the `apptainer` module:

```bash
$ module load apptainer
```

Now, any software image (`.sif`) file in the `/usr/local/usrapps/brc/brc_modules/images` directory can be run using the command `apptainer exec` which will temporarily load the software while your command is running. The basic structure is:

`apptainer exec <path_to_.sif> <command>`

For example, if we want to run `samtools` to print the help message:

```bash
$ apptainer exec /usr/local/usrapps/brc/brc_modules/images/quay.io_biocontainers_samtools:1.23.1--ha83d96e_0.sif samtools --help

Program: samtools (Tools for alignments in the SAM format)
Version: 1.23.1 (using htslib 1.23.1)

Usage:  samtools <command> [options]
...
```

::: {.callout-important}
Both options for loading and using BRC software are compatible with bash scripts and job submission. Never do computationally expensive work from the login nodes.
:::

### Bind paths and file visibility

Containers have their own isolated filesystem, so a program running inside one can only see host directories that have been "bound" (mounted) into it. A plain `apptainer exec` call adds no extra bind paths on its own — it relies entirely on Apptainer's default bind behavior. (You may notice an `Optional bind path (set BIND_PATH in your profile to enable)` comment in the module files; this is currently a placeholder and has no effect.)

By default, without any `--bind` flags, Apptainer automatically makes the following visible inside the container:

- your home directory (`$HOME`)
- the directory you run the command from (`$PWD`)
- `/tmp`, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`

The `module load` wrapper scripts add one more binding on top of that: every BRC tool module depends on the `singularity`/`apptainer` module, and that module's modulefile runs `prepend-path APPTAINER_BINDPATH $env(PWD),` when loaded. In practice this just re-asserts whatever directory you were in *at the moment you ran `module load`* — it does not track your directory afterward, and it is not scratch- or RS1-specific despite often looking that way if you happen to load modules from your scratch directory.

If the files you're working with (SAM/BAM files, reference genomes, etc.) live under one of those paths, everything works with no extra steps. If they live somewhere else — for example a scratch or RS1 path that isn't part of your current working directory tree — you have a few options:

1. **`cd` into the directory containing your files first**, then refer to them with relative paths. Since `$PWD` is auto-bound (both by Apptainer itself and by the `singularity`/`apptainer` module, per above), this is the simplest fix for a one-off command.
2. **Set the `APPTAINER_BINDPATH` environment variable.** Apptainer reads this variable automatically and applies it to every `exec`/`run`/`shell` call — including the ones inside the BRC `module load` wrapper scripts. This is the recommended fix if you regularly work with data outside your home directory, because it's a one-time setup that then applies to *every* BRC module:

    ```bash
    $ export APPTAINER_BINDPATH="/rs1,/share/$GROUP"
    ```

    Add this to your `~/.bashrc` to make it permanent. The value is a comma-separated list of `src[:dest[:opts]]` entries, same syntax as `--bind`.

::: {.callout-tip}
Bind at the group level (`/share/$GROUP`) rather than your own subdirectory (`/share/$GROUP/$USER`). Because the `singularity`/`apptainer` module also auto-binds `$PWD` (see above), if your own `APPTAINER_BINDPATH` entry is the *exact* directory you're sitting in when you load a module, Apptainer sees the same destination bound twice and prints a harmless but noisy warning:

```
WARNING: While bind mounting '/share/brc/sdweave2:/share/brc/sdweave2': destination is already in the mount point list
```

Binding the group root instead of your personal scratch directory still gives you access to everything under your own directory (permissions are unaffected — you see exactly what you could already see outside the container), but it's a different literal path than the one you're likely to actually `cd` into and load a module from, so the two bind entries stop colliding. The same logic applies to RS1: binding `/rs1` broadly avoids collisions with whatever project subdirectory you happen to be working in.
:::

3. **Bind the path explicitly for a single command** if you're calling `apptainer exec` yourself instead of going through a `module load` wrapper:

    ```bash
    $ apptainer exec --bind /path/to/data/dir /usr/local/usrapps/brc/brc_modules/images/<image>.sif samtools view ...
    ```

::: {.callout-tip}
If a tool reports that a file doesn't exist even though you can see it fine on the host filesystem (e.g. `[E::hts_open] fail to open file`), this is almost always a missing bind mount, not a typo in the path.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
The `Optional bind path (set BIND_PATH in your profile to enable)` comment you may see in the module files is currently a placeholder with no effect — use `APPTAINER_BINDPATH` above instead.
:::

## Requesting software

Perhaps you want to use a software package that is missing from the BRC library, or need a package updated to a newer version. Contact the BRC at ncstate_brc@ncsu.edu with:

1. Software package name
2. Link to software package
3. Specific software version (if applicable)

::: {.callout-note}
COMING SOON: Web form for software package requests.
:::
